nodes.title: SG-3 · Create coherent temporary pixel-art bedroom assets
nodes.body:
Context: game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room holds one flattened bedroom background, three furniture SVGs, three object SVGs, one idle-only boy sheet and one dust SVG. Desired behavior: separate layered files for background, furniture, objects, characters and effects are registered in manifest.json with dimensions, frames and animations, and a document lists replacement requirements. Expected result: manifest-driven, validated, no gray placeholders. Why: future cycles can swap individual assets.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the manifest, when loaded, then wall, floor, window and lighting background assets, five furniture assets, computer, books, door, window and secret door state assets, three boy sheets and dust and glow effects all exist as separate files
- Given a spritesheet entry, when validated, then frameCount matches the sheet dimensions and every animation frame index is valid
- Given the replacement document, when read, then it lists temporary-asset replacement requirements and does not claim production quality
- Given every manifest entry, when resolved, then it points to an existing file


## Scope
- In scope: SVG assets under game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room
- In scope: manifest.json entries
- In scope: schema validation of frames and animations
- In scope: replacement requirements document
- Out of scope: Phaser scene rendering changes
- Out of scope: backend changes
- Out of scope: production-quality artwork
- Preserve: existing manifest ids such as scene:bedroom, objects/bed and character:boy
- Preserve: existing manifest tests


## Technical constraints
- Use crisp pixel-art SVG (shape-rendering=crispEdges) with explicit integer width/height
- No gray rectangles as placeholders
- Manifest typed by zod schema in game/src/assets/manifest/schema.ts


## Definition of done
- All requirements delivered and unit tests green


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Schema rejects spritesheets whose frames or animations disagree with the sheet
nodes.body:
Context: assetSchema in game/src/assets/manifest/schema.ts only requires frames and dimensions for spritesheets. Desired behavior: superRefine also reports an issue when frameWidth*frameCount exceeds the width, frameHeight exceeds the height, or an animation frame index is >= frameCount. Expected result: invalid sheets fail parseManifest with path-named errors. Why: catch broken sheets early.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a spritesheet with frameCount 3 and width 64 and frameWidth 32, when parsed, then an issue at frames.frameCount is returned
- Given an animation referencing frame index 5 with frameCount 2, when parsed, then an issue at animations.<name>.frames is returned
- Given the committed manifest, when parsed, then it is ok


## Scope
- In scope: schema superRefine checks
- Out of scope: image decoding
- Preserve: existing error messages for missing frames/dimensions


## Technical constraints
- Must not throw; use ctx.addIssue


## Definition of done
- Schema checks implemented


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.description: Add dimension and animation index checks to the spritesheet superRefine.
acceptance_criteria: Over-wide frame counts are reported
Out-of-range animation frames are reported

steps.action: After the existing frames/dimensions checks, add: when both asset.frames and asset.dimensions are defined, if frames.frameWidth*frames.frameCount > dimensions.width add an issue at path ['frames','frameCount'] message 'frameCount exceeds sheet width'; if frames.frameHeight > dimensions.height add an issue at ['frames','frameHeight'] message 'frameHeight exceeds sheet height'; then for each [name, anim] of Object.entries(asset.animations ?? {}) if any frame >= frames.frameCount add an issue at ['animations', name, 'frames'] message 'animation frame out of range'. Also apply the animation check when type is not spritesheet is unnecessary; keep it spritesheet-only.
steps.code: if (asset.frames && asset.dimensions && asset.frames.frameWidth * asset.frames.frameCount > asset.dimensions.width) { ctx.addIssue({ code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom, path: ['frames','frameCount'], message: 'frameCount exceeds sheet width' }); }
steps.expected: Invalid sheets produce path-named issues; valid ones unchanged
